findings.premise: The design addresses both parts of the ISSUE's root cause/fix intent: (a) an install-success marker so a failed/interrupted npm install is retried instead of being permanently skipped, and (b) a CXXFLAGS fix letting fs-ext build against the Node 22.22.1 headers — using the exact C++ standard value ('-std=c++17') already decided and qualified with the project-memory package owner in Epic 17123b6d, as the ISSUE's fix intent (b) explicitly requires.
findings.evidence: ISSUE.md's fix intent (b) says the fix must be 'decided together with the owner of the project-memory package (Epic 17123b6d)'. The project-memory package's own already-qualified sources all use plain '-std=c++17': README.md:119 ('CXXFLAGS=-std=c++17 npm ci'), .github/workflows/project-memory.yml:46 (CXXFLAGS: -std=c++17), packed.test.ts:17 (CXXFLAGS: '-std=c++17'), and the owner-run qualification evidence (docs/epics/.../evidence/t2/qualification.json). The LLD's §3.2 and all its contract/postcondition text consistently specify '-std=c++17' (not a divergent value), so it reuses the owner-qualified value rather than inventing its own. [files: docs/standalone/daemon-update-never-retries-failed-npm-E20261102ca9883ca/ISSUE.md, packages/project-memory/README.md, .github/workflows/project-memory.yml, packages/project-memory/src/__tests__/packed.test.ts]
findings.action: None — the fix covers both root-cause parts and reuses the owner-qualified CXXFLAGS value.

findings.premise: Today, both update paths decide whether to run npm install purely from whether the lockfile hash changed across the pull or node_modules is missing, with no record of whether the last install actually succeeded — exactly as the design's 'State before' / root-cause section claims.
findings.evidence: src/cli/services/maintenance.ts:122-123: `const lockChanged = lockBefore !== lockAfter || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules')); if (opts.skipInstall !== true && lockChanged) { ... }` — no success/failure record. scripts/daemon-ctl.sh:115: `if [ -z "$lock_before" ] || [ "$lock_before" != "$lock_after" ] || [ ! -d "$DAEMON_SRC/node_modules" ]; then` mirrors this exactly, matching citations c1/c2. [files: src/cli/services/maintenance.ts, scripts/daemon-ctl.sh]
findings.action: None — the design's description of current behaviour is accurate.

The daemon itself never reimplements the pull/rebuild/restart sequence', so it delegates to daemon-ctl.sh rather than duplicating the install logic. findings.premise: The invariants the design promises to keep are real in the current code: a failed npm install still fails the update/script, lockfile churn from npm install is discarded before the cleanliness/fast-forward check in both update paths, skipInstall skips the install entirely, and the two installer copies are held byte-identical by an existing test.
findings.evidence: maintenance.ts:125-127 returns `{ ok: false, steps, error: 'npm install failed' }` on non-zero exit; daemon-ctl.sh:117 `die "npm install failed..." 4`. maintenance.ts:94-99 and daemon-ctl.sh:88-90 both run `git checkout -- package-lock.json` after fetch, before the dirty/fast-forward check, discarding install-time lockfile rewrites. installer-defs.test.ts:80 already asserts `assert.equal(read('vscode-plugin/assets/insrc-daemon-install.sh'), script)`. CAVEAT: the LLD's own footnote [[c2]] attached specifically to the lockfile-churn-discard invariant points to scripts/daemon-ctl.sh:111-121 (the install-decision function, npm_install_if_needed) rather than to the actual discard code at daemon-ctl.sh:88-90 (inside sync_repo) — a mislabeled citation, though the invariant it supports is independently true in the code. [files: src/cli/services/maintenance.ts, scripts/daemon-ctl.sh, src/config/__tests__/installer-defs.test.ts]
findings.action: Minor: re-point the [[c2]] footnote on the lockfile-churn-discard invariant to the actual discard code (daemon-ctl.sh:88-90 / maintenance.ts:94-99) instead of the install-decision lines; does not change the invariant's correctness.

findings.premise: The ac1/ac2 tests described (fake npm exits 1 then 0; an unchanged lockfile with a stale or missing marker still installs) would actually fail against today's unmodified code, because today's decision ignores install success/failure entirely.
findings.evidence: maintenance.ts:122 and daemon-ctl.sh:115 compute the install-skip decision purely from lockfile-hash-unchanged plus node_modules existing. Running the described sequence against unmodified code — fail, then retry with an unchanged lockfile and now-existing (partial) node_modules — would skip the second install, which is exactly the bug the ISSUE reproduces ('the update logs package-lock.json unchanged; skipping... every later update skips the install the same way'), so the designed test is a valid pre-fix-failing regression test. [files: src/cli/services/maintenance.ts, scripts/daemon-ctl.sh]
findings.action: None — the test design would correctly fail pre-fix and pass post-fix.

summary.prose: A daemon update installs dependencies again whenever the last install did not finish successfully, not only when the lockfile changed: a small marker inside node_modules records the lockfile it was installed from, and it exists only after a successful install. Every daemon install also asks the C++ compiler for C++17, so the project-memory package's file-locking dependency builds on the pinned Node 22 headers. The same rule applies on the TUI update path and the script path both IDE plugins use.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Make daemon update recover from a failed npm install

api.name: update
api.signature: export async function update(opts: UpdateOptions, onLog: LogFn): Promise<MaintenanceResult>

returns.meaning: Unchanged shape: { ok, steps, error? }; steps includes 'install' when an install ran.

errors.type: MaintenanceResult { ok: false, error: 'npm install failed' }
errors.condition: npm install exits non-zero; the install marker is absent afterwards, so the next update installs again

preconditions: DAEMON_ROOT is a daemon git checkout (unchanged check)
postconditions: The install runs when skipInstall is not set and the install marker is missing or does not hold the hash of the synced package-lock.json (the lockfile-changed and node_modules-missing cases are subsumed: either leaves the marker absent or stale)
Before npm install starts, the marker is removed; after npm install exits 0, the marker is written with the hash of the synced package-lock.json taken before the install
npm install runs with the environment's CXXFLAGS plus -std=c++17 (an existing CXXFLAGS value is kept, with the flag appended)
When the install is skipped the log says the marker matches the lockfile

dataModelChanges.entity: install marker (node_modules/.insrc-install-ok in the daemon checkout)
dataModelChanges.details: A plain-text file holding one line: the git blob hash (`git hash-object package-lock.json`) of the synced package-lock.json from which the last successful npm install ran. Absent = no successful install recorded (fresh checkout, failed or interrupted install, node_modules deleted). Written by update(), npm_install_if_needed and the first-time installer scripts after npm install exits 0; removed by update() and npm_install_if_needed before an install starts. Lives inside node_modules so removing node_modules removes it. Existing installs have no marker, so their next update installs once.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: + <DAEMON_ROOT>/node_modules/.insrc-install-ok : text, one line, the lockfile blob hash

dataModelChanges.details: Every npm install the daemon tooling runs (maintenance.update, daemon-ctl.sh, both installer copies) sets CXXFLAGS to the caller's CXXFLAGS with -std=c++17 appended, so native dependencies whose build files set no C++ standard compile against the Node 22.22.1 headers pinned in .npmrc. Packages that pin their own standard (tree-sitter's -std=c++17) keep building; the full install is verified in the build stage. The project-memory package and its fs-ext dependency are not changed. The flag value is -std=c++17, the value the project-memory package's owner (Epic 17123b6d) already decided and qualified: its README (packages/project-memory/README.md:119), CI (.github/workflows/project-memory.yml:46) and packed-install test (packages/project-memory/src/__tests__/packed.test.ts:17) all use CXXFLAGS=-std=c++17, and its qualification evidence passed with it [c10]. The daemon reuses that value rather than choosing its own; -std=c++17 was also probed to build and load fs-ext on 2026-11-02 [c8].

errorCases.scenario: npm install exits non-zero (a native build fails, the network drops)
errorCases.detection: update() sees the npm child's non-zero exit code; npm_install_if_needed sees the subshell's non-zero status
errorCases.response: Return { ok:false, error:'npm install failed' } / die with exit 4, as today; the marker was removed before the install and is not written
errorCases.userImpact: The update fails visibly; the next update installs again instead of skipping

errorCases.scenario: The install is interrupted (process killed, machine sleeps or loses power) after it started
errorCases.detection: No detection at the time; on the next update the marker is absent because it is removed before the install and written only after exit 0
errorCases.userImpact: One extra install on the next update; no permanently half-installed daemon

errorCases.scenario: The marker cannot be written after a successful install (read-only or full disk)
errorCases.detection: The write throws (update) or the redirect fails (daemon-ctl.sh)
errorCases.response: update() returns { ok:false, error } naming the marker write; daemon-ctl.sh dies with exit 4 and the log names it
errorCases.userImpact: The update reports failure even though packages are installed; the next update installs again, which is safe

errorCases.scenario: git hash-object of package-lock.json fails (file missing in the checkout)
errorCases.detection: Empty hash string from the git call
errorCases.response: Treat as no match: install, and write no marker for an empty hash, so the next update installs again
errorCases.userImpact: Installs every update until the lockfile exists; never skips wrongly

migration.stateBefore: Both update paths decide to install from the lockfile hash before vs after the sync, or a missing node_modules (src/cli/services/maintenance.ts:121-131; scripts/daemon-ctl.sh:111-121, per s1 bundles 1 and 2). No successful-install record exists, and npm install runs with the caller's environment unchanged, so fs-ext fails to build under npm's bundled node-gyp 11.5.0 (s1 bundle 5).
migration.stateAfter: Both update paths install when node_modules/.insrc-install-ok is absent or holds a different lockfile hash; the marker is removed before and written after a successful install. Every daemon npm install, including both installer copies, runs with -std=c++17 appended to CXXFLAGS. The installers write the marker too.

migrationSteps.action: Ship the new decision rule, marker handling and CXXFLAGS in maintenance.update and daemon-ctl.sh, and the CXXFLAGS plus marker write in both installer copies, together in one change.

No data migration: an existing install has no marker, so its first update after this change installs once (with the C++17 flag, which also repairs a daemon whose earlier install failed) and writes the marker.
Rolling back to the old code ignores the marker file; a leftover marker inside node_modules is harmless.

migration.backwardCompat: No public API change: update()'s options and result shape and daemon-ctl.sh's commands, flags and exit codes stay the same. The only visible differences are one extra install on the first update after the change, and an install whenever the previous one did not complete.

alternativesConsidered.name: Install marker keyed by the lockfile hash + C++17 CXXFLAGS at every daemon install site
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A marker file inside node_modules records the lockfile hash of the last successful install; updates install when it is absent or different, and every daemon npm install runs with -std=c++17 appended to CXXFLAGS.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Both update paths (maintenance.update and daemon-ctl.sh npm_install_if_needed) decide to install when the marker node_modules/.insrc-install-ok is missing or does not hold the hash of the synced (origin) package-lock.json, instead of comparing the before/after hashes. The marker is removed before an install starts and written only after npm install exits 0, so a failed or interrupted install leaves it absent and the next update installs again; deleting node_modules removes it too. The first-time installers write the same marker after their install. Every daemon npm install (the two update paths and both installer copies) runs with CXXFLAGS extended by -std=c++17 (keeping any CXXFLAGS the user set), so a native dependency whose build file sets no C++ standard (fs-ext) compiles against the Node 22.22.1 headers. The project-memory package and its fs-ext dependency are unchanged.
pros: Fixes both defects at the daemon's own install sites with no change to another epic's package
The marker is self-healing: any failure, interruption or manual node_modules deletion leads to a reinstall
Same rule and marker format in TypeScript and shell, testable with a fake npm
Existing installs without a marker reinstall once on their next update, which also repairs the currently broken installed daemon
cons: CXXFLAGS applies to every native build in the install; packages that pin their own -std (tree-sitter -std=c++17) must still build - verified in the build stage
A developer's own `npm install` outside these paths still needs CXXFLAGS (documented, not enforced)

alternativesConsidered.name: Install marker + a newer node-gyp pinned for npm
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Same marker for (a); for (b) point npm at node-gyp 13 (which adds -std=gnu++17) via a dev dependency and npm config.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The marker rule from a1 for the install decision. For the build, add node-gyp 13.x to the root package.json and set npm's node-gyp path to it in .npmrc, so every native build (including a developer's own npm install) uses the newer node-gyp that passes -std=gnu++17 from the Node 22 headers' common.gypi.
pros: Uses the build tool's own C++ standard handling instead of a flag
cons: Chicken-and-egg on a fresh checkout: the pinned node-gyp is not in node_modules until the first install, which is the install that needs it
The probe of npm_config_node_gyp pointing at node-gyp 13 failed to build fs-ext, so it is unproven
Adds a dependency and a path-dependent npm setting
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: fi-b and fi-d only partial: the first install cannot use a node-gyp it has not installed yet.

alternativesConsidered.name: Retry flag on failure only + patch fs-ext
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Record a failed install (a flag file) to force the next install, and patch fs-ext's binding.gyp to request C++17.
alternativesConsidered.approach: On a non-zero npm install exit, write a 'last install failed' flag; the next update installs when the flag exists. For fs-ext, apply a patch (patch-package or an npm override to a fork) adding a C++17 flag to its binding.gyp.
pros: Smallest change to the decision logic
cons: An interrupted install (killed process, power loss) writes no flag, so the skip-forever case stays
Patching or forking fs-ext changes the project-memory package's dependency, owned by another epic, and adds a patch toolchain
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates fi-c and only partially meets fi-a.
